lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: documenting a maintenance request

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic documenting a maintenance request task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner picks one real or realistic maintenance issue from their own household (or a provided example if none currently exists), first writes a rough draft, then revises it into a complete maintenance-request note following a four-part structure, practicing the documentation skill without contacting any real outside party.
safetyNotes: This note is a writing and documentation exercise only; it is never sent to any real landlord, employer, property manager, or other outside party as part of this lesson.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l06-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l06-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l06-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l06-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: What specifically changed between your rough draft and your final note, and why does that specific change make the note more useful to whoever eventually reads it?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u02-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Note completeness: Note includes all four required parts clearly and in a logical order. | Specificity and urgency accuracy: The broken item is named specifically, and the urgency level has a clear, specific one-sentence reason. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner write a second maintenance-request note for a lower-urgency issue and explain what specifically in the wording signals the lower urgency compared to their first note.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic documenting a maintenance request task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or a document
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: documenting a maintenance request worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner picks one real or realistic maintenance issue from their own household (or a provided example if none currently exists), first writes a rough draft, then revises it into a complete maintenance-request note following a four-part structure, practicing the documentation skill without contacting any real outside party.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact documenting a maintenance request decision or action.

Model move 2: Without worrying about structure yet, quickly write down a maintenance issue from your household (or use this example: 'the kitchen faucet drips constantly, even when fully shut off') exactly as you'd first think to describe it.

Model move 3: Compare your rough draft to the four required parts of a maintenance-request note: what's broken (a specific item, not just 'it's broken'), the exact location, how long it's been happening, and an urgency level (routine, needs attention soon, or urgent).

Model check: Note completeness: Note includes all four required parts clearly and in a logical order. | Specificity and urgency accuracy: The broken item is named specifically, and the urgency level has a clear, specific one-sentence reason.

resources.title: documenting a maintenance request action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for documenting a maintenance request.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: documenting a maintenance request coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner picks one real or realistic maintenance issue from their own household (or a provided example if none currently exists), first writes a rough draft, then revises it into a complete maintenance-request note following a four-part structure, practicing the documentation skill without contacting any real outside party.

Coach direction: Without worrying about structure yet, quickly write down a maintenance issue from your household (or use this example: 'the kitchen faucet drips constantly, even when fully shut off') exactly as you'd first think to describe it.
Learner prompt: Write your rough, first-pass description of the issue in one or two sentences.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: documenting a maintenance request complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Compare your rough draft to the four required parts of a maintenance-request note: what's broken (a specific item, not just 'it's broken'), the exact location, how long it's been happening, and an urgency level (routine, needs attention soon, or urgent).
Response 1 (t2-p1): My rough draft names the specific broken item, not just a vague problem.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My rough draft is missing at least one of the four required parts.
Response 3 (t2-p3): Which of the four parts (what's broken, exact location, how long, urgency) was missing or weakest in your rough draft?
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: documenting a maintenance request minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: What specifically changed between your rough draft and your final note, and why does that specific change make the note more useful to whoever eventually reads it?

Success checks: Note completeness: Note includes all four required parts clearly and in a logical order. | Specificity and urgency accuracy: The broken item is named specifically, and the urgency level has a clear, specific one-sentence reason.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: documenting a maintenance request supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l06-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u02-l06-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional documenting a maintenance request condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Note completeness: Note includes all four required parts clearly and in a logical order. | Specificity and urgency accuracy: The broken item is named specifically, and the urgency level has a clear, specific one-sentence reason..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l06-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: documenting a maintenance request — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the documenting a maintenance request task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
